Hi Laura,

Thanks for agreeing to share Secure SDLC materials as part of our SIG questionnaire review. To complete the assessment we need the following artifacts by EOD Thursday (2026-07-23):

- Recent code-review audit (last 6 months) showing PR approvals and merge protections
- CI/CD pipeline config and evidence of protected pipelines (logs or run IDs)
- Secrets management overview (how secrets are stored/rotated; KMS/HSM integration)
- Change management log showing deployments and approvals for production-impacting changes
- Your PR/review policy doc and a brief narrative on reviewer/approver assignment rules

If you can provide an index + the artifacts (stubs are fine), we can map them to SIG/CAT questions. Let me know if this timeline is feasible.

Best,

1) On reviewer assignment: can you provide the short narrative Laura mentioned that explains reviewer rotation and escalation for production change PRs?
2) For change-management: a single-line summary of approvals (e.g., "Code Owner + Release Manager required for production") would help our scoring.

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Secure development artifacts for assessor — SIG/SOC2 packet

Emily — thanks for the quick review. Attached are the three items you asked for in the body below and as separate short docs in the bundle:

1) Reviewer/Approver narrative (summary):
- For production-impacting PRs, two approvers are required: a designated code owner and a release manager. Code owner is typically the most recent owner of the module touched; reviewer rotation is enforced by team-level on-call schedules and quarterly reviewer audits. Escalation to Engineering Ops occurs if a PR stalls beyond 48 hours.

2) Change-management single-line summary:
- "Production deploys require Code Owner + Release Manager approvals; emergency deploys require Release Manager + Engineering Lead sign-off and are logged in change-management-log with emergency flag."

3) KMS tenancy confirmation:
- Keys are provisioned in Redwood's security account (separate AWS account dedicated to key management). We have a cross-account usage policy for runtime roles; ARNs were masked in the manifest to avoid publishing account IDs.

If you need a short diagram or a sample approval flow, I can patch that into the bundle this afternoon. Otherwise, please confirm this satisfies your questions and we will mark the ticket ACME-SIG-1127 as ready for mapping.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
